subject: [PATCH RFC v4 03/12] mm: rename get_user_page_vma_remote() to get_user_page_lookup_vma()

2026-07-24.patch_summary: This patch renames the function get_user_page_vma_remote() to get_user_page_lookup_vma() in the Linux kernel's memory management (mm) module. The renamed function still faults in a page at the specified address and looks up the VMA that covers it, but now with a more descriptive name that reflects its purpose of looking up the VMA. This change is intended to improve code readability and does not introduce any functional changes. The patch affects several files in the kernel, including arch-specific code and header files.

reviews.author: Suren Baghdasaryan
reviews.summary:
The reviewer suggested adding a brief explanation of the patch's purpose before describing its results, noting that the title already conveys the rename operation.

reviews.raw_body:
nit: Before explaining the results we usually state what this patch is
doing. I know the title alread says "rename get_user_page_vma_remote()
to get_user_page_lookup_vma()" but it seems appropriate to say that
here too.

2026-07-27.patch_summary: This patch renames the function get_user_page_vma_remote() to get_user_page_lookup_vma(). The renamed function still faults in a page at the specified address and looks up the VMA that covers it, but does so in a remote memory management context. This change is intended to simplify the namespace for adding a variant of this function where the caller already has the VMA. No functional changes are made by this patch.
